name: DoE Planner
description: Design of Experiments: Full Factorial, Fractional, Plackett-Burman, CCD, Box-Behnken, Taguchi
whenToUse: When the effect of several factors on one or more responses is to be studied in a planned experiment: full or fractional factorial, Plackett-Burman, response surface (CCD, Box-Behnken), Taguchi or optimal (D, A, G), also as an EVOP project over several phases. Which design type fits is settled beforehand in the DoE advisor (doe-advisor).
analysisIncomplete: Please fill in all response values in the worksheet first ({pct}% filled).
analysisSingular: Model cannot be computed (singular matrix). Check your data.
tip_full: All factor combinations are tested. For 2-level factors: 2^k runs; for mixed levels: product of all level counts. Ideal for few factors (2–4) when all main effects and interactions are needed.
tip_frac: Only a fraction of combinations is tested (2^(k−p) runs). Saves runs with many factors, at the cost of confounding some interactions.
tip_pb:
Screening design with resolution III. Very efficient for identifying the few significant factors out of many.

When to use:
• Many factors (7–47) but limited experimental budget
• Goal: identify the 3–5 most important factors (Pareto principle)
• Early project phase — the question is 'which factors matter?', not 'how exactly do they interact?'
• Runs = next multiple of 4 above the factor count → e.g. 12 runs for 11 factors

When NOT to use:
• Interactions matter — PB confounds main effects with 2-factor interactions (resolution III)
• Precise effect estimation needed — use 2^(k−p) with resolution ≥ V instead
• Few factors (≤ 5) — a full factorial is often more economical and provides clean interaction estimates
• Nonlinear effects expected — PB has only 2 levels, no curvature check

Typical workflow:
1. PB screening → find significant factors
2. Fix non-significant factors at their economical level
3. Follow-up design (2^k or CCD) with remaining factors for detailed modeling
tip_ccd: Central Composite Design for response surface modeling. Enables quadratic models and optimization.
tip_bb: Box-Behnken design: 3-level, no extreme points (corners). Ideal when extreme combinations must be avoided. Requires 3–7 factors.
tip_taguchi: Taguchi orthogonal array: Robust design with few runs. Focus on signal-to-noise ratio and robustness.
tip_dopt: D-optimal design: Maximizes the determinant of X'X (information matrix). Minimizes the volume of the confidence ellipsoid for all parameter estimates.
tip_aopt: A-optimal design: Minimizes the trace of (X'X)⁻¹. Minimizes the average variance of all parameter estimates.
tip_gopt: G-optimal design: Minimizes the maximum prediction variance across the design space. Ensures uniform prediction quality.
tipTwoLevelOnly: This design is only available for factors with exactly 2 levels. Reduce the number of levels or choose a different design (e.g. Full Factorial, Box-Behnken, or Taguchi).
optimalInfo_dopt: D-optimal designs maximize the determinant of the information matrix, providing the most precise overall parameter estimates for a given number of runs.
optimalInfo_aopt: A-optimal designs minimize the average variance of parameter estimates. They provide the best average precision across all model coefficients.
optimalInfo_gopt: G-optimal designs minimize the maximum prediction variance. They ensure the most uniform prediction quality across the entire design space.
optimalMinRunsNew: Minimum: {min} additional runs on top of the {m} existing rows.
tipOptimalQuadratic: Include squared terms (x²) in the model. Requires more runs but enables quadratic response surface modeling.
optimalTooFewRuns: Too few runs — at least {min} are needed for the selected model.
optimalTooFewRunsNew: Too few additional runs — at least {min} are needed on top of the {m} existing rows.
forbiddenHint: Factor-level combinations that are physically impossible or unwanted. The optimiser avoids them. "Any" leaves the factor unconstrained for that rule.
modelTermsHint: Interactions known to be physically decoupled can be excluded from the model. That lowers the minimum run count and improves precision of the remaining effects.
modelTermsHintHier: Pick every term the model should contain. Marginality is enforced: a higher-order term pulls in all of its subterms; turning off a main effect cascades out every interaction that contained it.
previewHint: Temporary — adjust factor values or pre-fill responses. Only "Create datasheet" turns this into a real datasheet.
previewStaleNote: Factor values were edited manually — the reported optimality score refers to the original suggestion and is no longer guaranteed for the edited values.
worksheetCreateHint: A datasheet is only created after confirmation. Measurement results will then be entered there.
worksheetStaleWarning: The design has changed — the linked datasheet no longer matches the current plan. "Recreate" discards the old datasheet.
bbNotAvailable: Box-Behnken is not available for k={k} (supported: {min}–{max} factors).
fracNotAvailable: No fractional factorial designs available for k={k} factors (supported: {min}–{max}).
taguchiNotAvailable: No suitable Taguchi array for k={k} factors with {levels} levels available.
recFull: For {k} factors (2-level), a full factorial design is recommended.
recFrac: For {k} factors, a fractional factorial design is recommended.
recPB: For many factors ({k}), a Plackett-Burman screening is ideal.
recBB: For 3-level factors, a Box-Behnken design is recommended.
recTaguchi: For 3-level factors, a Taguchi array is a good choice.
resLegendFull: Full factorial — all main effects and interactions independently estimable.
resLegendVII: Main effects and 2-factor interactions not aliased with 4-factor or lower interactions.
resLegendVI: Main effects not aliased with 4-factor interactions; 2-factor interactions not aliased with 3-factor interactions.
resLegendV: Main effects and 2-factor interactions independently estimable; 2-factor interactions aliased with 3-factor interactions.
resLegendIV: Main effects not aliased with 2-factor interactions; 2-factor interactions aliased with each other.
resLegendIII: Main effects aliased with 2-factor interactions — screening designs only.
factorUnitCategoricalDisabled: Categorical factors carry no physical unit.
tipRandomize:
Randomization protects against systematic nuisance variables (e.g. fatigue, temperature drift, material batches). RECOMMENDED in most cases.

Do NOT randomize when:
• Changeover between factor levels is very costly or time-consuming (e.g. furnace temperature)
• Split-plot designs are intentionally used
• EVOP is running and sequence must be fixed

Rule of thumb: when in doubt, always randomize.
tipReplicates:
Replication repeats the entire design 1:1. Each factor combination is run multiple times under identical conditions.

Benefits:
• Provides an independent estimate of pure error (repeatability)
• Increases statistical power for detecting effects
• Enables lack-of-fit testing for the regression model

Rule of thumb:
• 1 replicate = no replication (screening phase, limited budget)
• 2 replicates = standard for confirmatory experiments
• 3+ replicates = high-precision studies or noisy processes
tipCenterPoints:
Center points are replicates at the midpoint of all factors (all levels set to their center value).

Benefits:
• Estimate pure experimental error (Replicate Error) — without them, unreplicated 2^k designs have no independent error estimate
• Curvature check — if the center mean deviates significantly from the model prediction, quadratic effects are present
• Efficient: only 3 extra runs for both benefits

When to use:
• RECOMMENDED for 2^k and fractional factorial designs without other replicates
• Not needed for CCD (has its own center points) or Box-Behnken
factorLevelsError: Please set at least the low and high level for all factors.
selectResError: Please select a design from the table.
stepEvaluateDesc: Evaluate design quality before running experiments: efficiency, confounding (aliases), variance inflation factors, and statistical power.
noEvaluation: Please generate an experiment design first.
tipDEff: D-Efficiency: Measures precision of parameter estimation. 100% = optimal design. Based on the determinant of X'X.
tipAEff: A-Efficiency: Measures average estimation accuracy of all parameters. Based on the trace of (X'X)^-1.
tipGEff: G-Efficiency: Ratio of average to maximum prediction variance. 100% = uniform prediction quality.
tipCondNum: Condition number: Measure of numerical stability. Ideally close to 1. Values >1000 indicate collinearity.
tipMaxLev: Maximum leverage: Largest influence of any single design point on the estimate. Ideal: p/n.
tipVIF: VIF measures how much a coefficient's variance is inflated due to correlation with other predictors. VIF=1 = perfectly orthogonal. VIF>5 = concerning → adjust the design (add more runs or choose a higher resolution). VIF>10 = severe multicollinearity → fundamentally change the design, or drop the confounded terms from the model during regression analysis.
tipAlias: Shows which effects are confounded (aliased) in a fractional factorial design. Aliased effects cannot be estimated independently.
noAliases: No confounding — all effects are independently estimable (full factorial design).
tipPower: Statistical power: probability of detecting an effect of a given size. Power ≥ 80% is generally considered adequate.
powerDesc: n={n} runs, df(Error)={dfError}, α={alpha}. Power for various standardized effect sizes (Δ/σ):
powerSaturated: Power cannot be computed: the model is saturated (df(Error) = 0). Add replicates or reduce the model.
decisionDesc: What should happen after this analysis?
decisionConfirm_repeat: Repeat this phase? A new cycle with the same factor settings will be created.
decisionConfirm_recenter: Re-center? The best point becomes the new center. Factor levels will be adjusted automatically.
decisionConfirm_stop: Complete the project? No further phases will be created.
evopRec_repeat: Recommendation: Repeat cycle — no significant effects detected yet.
evopRec_recenter: Recommendation: Re-center — significant effects detected. Use the best point as the new center.
evopRec_stop: Recommendation: Complete — no significant effects after multiple cycles. Process is stable.
configureLeft: Configure factors, responses, and design type in the left panel.
augmentHint: Appends additional optimal runs to the linked datasheet. Already-conducted runs stay unchanged; only the new rows are chosen D/A/G-optimally.
sourceHint: Columns are matched to factors and responses by name. Existing runs are kept as fixed rows; only the additional runs are chosen optimally.
sourceMappingOk: {rows} runs will be reused, {responses} response column(s) detected.
sourceSkipped: ({n} row(s) skipped — missing or invalid values.)
sourceMissingFactors: No columns found for these factors: {names}.
tipDispersion: Models the mean and ln(s²) as two separate responses — identifies factor settings that reduce process variability independently of the mean (dual-response approach after Vining & Myers). Requires at least 2 replicates per design point.
dispersionNoReplicates: Dispersion analysis requires at least 2 replicates per design point. Increase the replicates option in the left panel or add repeat runs in the worksheet.
dispersionZeroVar: {n} design point(s) with variance = 0 (all replicates identical) — these are excluded from the log-s² model.
dispersionModelNotFitted: Model could not be fitted (too few points or singular).
dispersionNoModel: No log-s² model available — all design points had variance = 0 or too few usable points.
dispersionConclusionNone: No factors with significant dispersion effect detected — process variability does not appear to be controllable through the investigated factors. Check other sources (measurement system, raw material, environment).
dispersionPreferInteraction: Interaction effect — read level combination from contour plot

invariants.minResponses: The plan needs at least one response.
invariants.validSelection: The resolution and Plackett-Burman choice must fit the number of factors and the design type; multi-level factors rule out the fractional and Plackett-Burman design types.
invariants.uniqueFactorIds: Every factor needs an id of its own.
invariants.analysisResponse: The analysis response must be one of the existing responses.
invariants.activePhase: The active phase must be an existing phase, or −1 outside project mode.

confirm.completePhase: Complete the active phase with the decision “{decision}”? The decision cannot be changed afterwards.

generateFailed: The design could not be generated.
datasheetFailed: The datasheet could not be created.
augmentFailed: The design could not be augmented.
transferFailed: The data could not be handed to the regression.
needsCurrentDatasheet: The datasheet no longer fits the plan; create it again first.
needsOptimal: Only optimal designs (D, A, G) can be extended.
reshuffleTitle: Draw a new run order: otherwise the same configuration always gives the same plan.
